title: Activation Conductivity — Roadmap Lattice, KPI Tracker & Capacity Probe
content:
Summary:
This is a working instrument for an upcoming feature activation that stitches together: roadmap lattice (phase + dependency map), a compact KPI tracker (leading/lagging) and a scheduled capacity probe plan (traffic experiments + failover checks). Purpose is to give PMs/EngOps a single living canvas to run preflight decisions and to hand off to SRE/Hosted API operations for go/no-go.

Top-level goals:
- Safe first-1k customers pilot; measurable latency and cost guards.
- Keep onboarding token burn < projected by 25% via caching + batching.
- Zero-customer-visible regression (>=99.9% success within service goals) during canary traffic.

Definitions (quick):
- Conductivity score: composite 0-100 that captures how well traffic flows through routing+cache. High conductivity => fewer cache misses + smaller tail latency.
- Capacity probe: time-boxed traffic ramp used to validate batching, autoscale, and KV cache hit ratios at target QPS.
- Traffic circuit: a scoped set of routes and customers used in a probe.

KPI lattice (owner and target):
- Latency P95 (ms): owner: Jun Park; pilot target: <180 ms; ramp target: <160 ms
- Latency P99 (ms): owner: Jun Park; pilot target: <350 ms; ramp target: <300 ms
- Error rate (5xx per 10k): owner: Marco Diaz; pilot target: <5; ramp target: <2
- Token cost per request (USD): owner: Aisha Patel; pilot target: <= $0.0045; ramp target: <= $0.0038
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV): owner: SRE lead; pilot target: >=45%; ramp target: >=60%
- Throughput (req/sec): owner: Eng Ops; probe target: 1500 rps sustained for 10m
- User-facing regressions (qualitative): owner: PM; pilot target: 0 critical regressions

Leading indicators to watch during probes:
- Median request queue time at frontend (ms) — rises before P95 spikes.
- Active GPU utilization % and GPU mem fragmentation sign (kernel stalls).
- Batching efficiency: average tokens per batch (lower => higher cost).
- KV eviction rate and average TTL hit.

Rollout phases & gating (condensed):
- Phase 0: Dry-run in staging (internal only) — pass smoke + correctness tests. Gate: all e2e tests green.
- Phase 1: Canary (3%) — run 1 rolling 2h capacity probe. Gate: P95 < pilot target, error rate within limit, cache hit ratio within 10% of goal.
- Phase 2: Incremental ramp (3->30%) — repeated 15m probes at key steps (3, 10, 30%). Gate: each probe must meet gating signal for 30m window.
- Phase 3: Broad open (100%) — monitor for 4h high-fidelity telemetry; fallback ramps if sustained degradation.

Capacity probe calendar (examples):
- Probe A: 2025-02-10 09:00 UTC, traffic circuit: onboarding-flow-v1, target 600 rps for 10m, owner: Eng Ops (K. Malik)
- Probe B: 2025-02-12 16:00 UTC, traffic circuit: chronic-query-set, target 1500 rps for 10m, owner: Jun Park
- Warm-up: 10m warm-up at 30% of target before each probe to populate caches; always verify prefix cache hit ratio > 30% before starting main window.

Readiness checklist (pre-probe):
- [ ] Canary model pinned and checksum verified (owner: ML Ops).
- [ ] Rollback model variant prep (owner: Model Platform).
- [ ] Autoscale policy reviewed with SRE (owner: Eng Ops).
- [ ] Readout dashboards created: latency P50/P95/P99, error breakdown, token cost approximation, cache hit curve (owner: Observability).
- [ ] Incident playbook staged in #incident-activation and on-call notified (owner: SRE lead).
- [ ] Customer comms draft ready (owner: PM).
- [ ] Safety throttle op in API gateway configured (owner: Infra).

Contingency plays (short):
- Fast fallback: shift traffic to previous stable model variant + auto-scale down new variant. Command: rollout controller -> set trafficWeight=0 for new variant. (owner: Eng Ops).
- Token shock limiter: globally cap tokens/sec for activation cohort if token cost burn > 30% over projection for 10m. (owner: Billing/Platform).
- Graceful degrade: switch to low-latency model family (quantized) for affected route if P99 > threshold for 5m. (owner: Serving Runtime).

Risk register (brief):
- R1: Cache warm-up takes longer than expected -> mitigation: extended warm-up window and pre-warm synthetic prefix requests (owner: Observability).
- R2: Kernel stall on a specific model shape under 4096 context -> mitigation: run small kernel sweep in staging + emergency kernel pinning (owner: Serving Runtime).
- R3: Unexpected token burn due to misconfigured prompt -> mitigation: instrument prompt length guardrails and per-request token estimator (owner: Developer Experience).

Quick KPI tracker snapshot (to paste into sheet):
Columns: date | probe | phase | route | owner | p50 | p95 | p99 | error_per_10k | cache_hit_% | tokens_per_req | cost_per_req | notes
Row example: 2025-02-10 | Probe A | Phase1 | onboarding-flow-v1 | Jun Park | 72 | 158 | 310 | 3 | 52 | 420 | $0.0042 | warmed, minor eviction spike

Ops commands & markers (notes to Eng Ops):
- Before probe: tag traces with activation=conductivity-x for quick filter.
- During probe: set short-lived alert at p95>200ms with 10m suppression window to avoid noisy flaps.
- Post-probe: run diff of token cost by customer cohort (billing delta).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: acceptable window for cache hit ramp during Phase1: 10m vs 30m? (ops tradeoffs).
- Q2: how to handle feature flags for private-deploy customers (if their model variants are pinned) — do we run separate probes per private deployment?
- Q3: do we include embeddings routes in the same probe or standalone probes (embedding workload has different token shapes).

Next steps (this doc owner: Evelyn Chen):
- Resolve Q1 in sync call with SRE + Observability (invite list: SRE, Observability, Serving Runtime) — target 2025-02-03.
- Finalize probe calendar and publish to #launch-readiness by 2025-02-05.
- Convert KPI snapshot to a live sheet and wire the Cost-per-request estimate to Billing test project.

Notes to self (scratch):
- If probe pushes P99 close to 400ms, consider early stop and collect heap/memtrace dump.
- Remember to update rollout-controller doc with new trafficWeight param examples.

References and links (in-text):
- Confluence playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/activation-playbook
- Probe runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/88
- Related Jira: JIRA-6123 (activation runbook)

End of working canvas. This is intentionally 'shorthand' — expand into the final launch checklist once gating decisions are firm.
